title: MCP server manifest (C6)
description: Generated by the starter at build time (target/mcp-manifest.json) or built at startup from the server's tools/list (CC-140), served by every server at GET /.well-known/mcp-manifest (C14, without authentication) and pulled by the gateway when the server is added, on refresh and in its runtime loop (C5, 'Manifest intake'; CC-249). Rules checked in addition to this schema (see README, 'Reguły semantyczne'): serverId == 'mcp-' + system; tool names unique; every resourceRefs[].type and resourceTypes[].parent is declared in resourceTypes; resourceTypes[].type unique, all in one Cedar namespace that equals policies.namespace; each declaration consistent (parent and parentAttribute together, parent in the same namespace, earlyScopeCheck only with a scopePattern, the classification attribute among attributes, idPattern and scopePattern anchored with ^ and $ without a top-level alternation); policies.files names unique; policiesHash recomputed from policies and resourceTypes equals the declared one; definition.name == name; definition.inputSchema has no confirmation_code and is closed and bounded (CC-078, CC-123: type object and additionalProperties false at every object level, no open maps, every string with maxLength unless an enum or const, every array with maxItems and items, every number with minimum and maximum, patterns anchored with ^ and $, every node typed, no allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/if/then/else); definitionHash recomputed from definition and the entry equals the declared one (CC-005). Since 8.0.0 (CC-258, CC-262): resources, resourceTemplates and prompts with the rules resources-valid, resource-templates-valid, prompts-valid, resource-uri-scheme, resource-names-unique, resource-uri-unambiguous, uri-template-level1, uri-variables-bound, uri-template-entity-variable and prompt-placeholders-declared; the second part of a resource type is not a name of the base schema (resource-type-name-reserved); a valueOnly type is used only in variables[].type and argumentRules[].type, never in resourceRefs; the hash of a resource, a template and a prompt is recomputed like that of a tool (see README, 'Registry and definition pinning').

environment.description: Environment the server was built for (CC-138). Absent means production. A gateway in production mode rejects a manifest with dev (422 manifest_rejected, reason environment_mismatch). Not part of any definitionHash.

internalUrl.description: Informational and optional (CC-249): the gateway connects to the address an administrator gave it and ignores this one.

tools.description: Which of the two entry forms applies depends on source: AdapterToolEntry when source is adapter, ToolEntry otherwise (CC-193). Since 8.0.0 the array may be empty when the manifest has resources, resourceTemplates or prompts (at least one of the four lists is not empty).

contractsVersion.description: Version of mcp-contracts the server was built against (CC-258). Absent means 7.x or older. The gateway reads it to decide which claims and fields a server accepts; it is not part of any definitionHash.

resources.description: Static resources of the server (CC-258): catalog documents whose content comes from the server, not from the account of the user. Names are unique together with resourceTemplates.

resourceTemplates.description: Resource templates of the server (CC-258): a URI template with variables bound to resource types.

prompts.description: Prompts of the server (CC-258): a static catalog pinned by definitionHash, messages included. The gateway builds the result of prompts/get from it and never calls the server. An adapter has none.

source.description: Absent for a server built on the starter. adapter marks the manifest of an adapter, the sidecar of a foreign MCP server (CC-193): its tool entries carry no risk and no action (an administrator classifies them at approval, outside definitionHash) and no resourceRefs, no resourceTypes and no policies (its policies are its own, outside the platform).

policies.description: The policy fragment of the server (C7), from src/main/resources/mcp/policies/ of its repository: the Cedar schema of its one namespace and its resource policies. Present for a server built on the starter, absent for an adapter. It is validated at registration (base schema plus fragment compose and validate in strict mode, see cedar/entity-builder.md) and is part of what an administrator approves (policiesHash).

namespace.description: The Cedar namespace of the server; every resourceTypes[].type starts with it.

schema.description: Text of schema.cedarschema: exactly one namespace, the server's own.

files.description: The *.cedar files of the server, in file name order.

policiesHash.description: sha256 over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of {"policies": <policies>, "resourceTypes": <resourceTypes>} (see test-vectors/policies-hash): a change of a declaration (earlyScopeCheck, idPattern, scopePattern, classification) needs approval like a change of a policy. The gateway recomputes it; a changed hash of a deployed server puts the server in pending_approval until an administrator approves it. Present exactly when policies is.

ResourceTypeDeclaration.description: Everything the entity builder knows about a resource type of this server; there is no built-in type (cedar/entity-builder.md). A type with valueOnly true only limits a value (a file path, a ref): it has just type and idPattern, no entity and no attributes.

valueOnly.description: True: the type has no Cedar entity, no scopes and no resolver; it may appear only in variables[].type of a resource template and argumentRules[].type of a prompt, never in resourceRefs (CC-258). Allowed members then: type, idPattern and valueOnly.

attributes.description: Attributes the server's resolver fills from the system (Cedar entity attributes), without the parent attribute and without scopes, which the builder adds.

parent.description: Type of the containing resource, declared in this manifest, same namespace.

parentAttribute.description: Cedar attribute that holds the parent entity; required with parent and only then.

idPattern.description: Anchored regular expression (^...$, no top-level alternation) of the ids of this type: tool arguments, resolved resources. Written in the subset that Java and ECMAScript share; matched against the whole id.

scopePattern.description: Anchored regular expression of the local part of a grantable scope id (<Type>/<local part>). Absent: the type cannot be granted in the scope mapping.

earlyScopeCheck.description: Whether the gateway checks tool arguments of this type against the scopes of the user before the call (context.refs). Only for types whose scope is the exact id; requires scopePattern.

classification.description: The attribute the builder normalizes (trim, ASCII lower case, sets without duplicates); a resource missing a required one is refused (internal_error).

argument.description: Name of a top-level argument of the tool's inputSchema whose value is a resource id (string or array of strings).

ToolEntry.description: Manifest entry of one tool. Every tool that accepts a resource identifier MUST declare resourceRefs (C6).

ToolEntryFields.description: Fields of a manifest tool entry, open for composition (used by the gateway registry API). risk and action are required by ToolEntry and forbidden by AdapterToolEntry.

additionalGroup.description: Optional group (C9) that a user needs in addition to the group the risk derives: mcp-<system>-<suffix> with the system of this server and a suffix other than read, write and destructive (checked by the rule additional-group-valid), for example mcp-opensearch-ops for an ops-only tool. It can only narrow access (platform-call-additional-group); the risk-derived group is still needed. Part of definitionHash, so a change needs approval. Not allowed in an adapter manifest.

resourceRefs.description: Always present; an empty array when the tool takes no resource identifier (one canonical form for definitionHash).

definitionHash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of definition + risk, action, resourceRefs + system, credential (CC-004, CC-005). Receivers recompute it.

McpToolDefinition.description: Full MCP tool definition as returned by tools/list (CC-005). Input of definitionHash together with risk, action, resourceRefs and the server fields system and credential. title is required (CC-115) and hashed like description (CC-042); icons and _meta are not allowed in v1, because they would reach the client without being pinned.

title.description: Display name shown by MCP clients; required since 3.0.0 (CC-115) and part of definitionHash (CC-042).

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the arguments. Must not declare confirmation_code (reserved for the gateway, C11). Closed and bounded (CC-078, CC-123); checked by the semantic rules, because JSON Schema cannot express them for arbitrary nesting.

AdapterToolEntry.description: Manifest entry of a tool of an adapter (CC-193). The adapter does not classify: risk and action are absent (the administrator gives them at approval), resourceRefs is empty (policies are per tool), and definitionHash covers the definition, resourceRefs, system and credential without risk and action.

McpResourceDefinition.description: MCP resource definition as returned by resources/list (CC-258): name, title, description, uri and optionally mimeType and annotations. No size, icons or _meta, as in McpToolDefinition: they would reach the client without being pinned. Every member is part of definitionHash.

ResourceEntry.description: Manifest entry of a static resource (CC-258). The gateway does not call the credential broker for it and the server gets no credential, so the content cannot come from the account of the user.

additionalGroup.description: Optional group (C9) that a user needs in addition to the group the risk derives: mcp-<system>-<suffix> with the system of this server and a suffix other than read, write and destructive (checked by the rule additional-group-valid), for example mcp-opensearch-ops for an ops-only tool. It can only narrow access (platform-call-additional-group); the risk-derived group is still needed. Part of definitionHash, so a change needs approval. Not allowed in an adapter manifest.

definitionHash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of kind, the members of definition, the entry fields and system, credential (CC-258). Receivers recompute it.

AdapterResourceEntry.description: Manifest entry of a static resource of an adapter (CC-258): no additionalGroup (an administrator classifies at approval). The uri is as the client sees it, with the <system>+ prefix of the scheme.

definitionHash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of kind, the members of definition, the entry fields and system, credential (CC-258). Receivers recompute it.

McpResourceTemplateDefinition.description: MCP resource template definition as returned by resources/templates/list (CC-258). Every member is part of definitionHash.

ResourceTemplateVariable.description: A variable of a URI template bound to a resource type: the value must match the idPattern of the type. At least one variable of a template has a type with an entity (rule uri-template-entity-variable).

AdapterTemplateVariable.description: A variable of the URI template of an adapter (CC-258): an adapter declares no resourceTypes, so the variable carries its own bounds.

pattern.description: Anchored regular expression (^...$, no top-level alternation) matched against the whole value.

ResourceTemplateEntry.description: Manifest entry of a resource template (CC-258).

variables.description: One entry per variable of uriTemplate, in the order of first occurrence (rule uri-variables-bound).

additionalGroup.description: Optional group (C9) that a user needs in addition to the group the risk derives: mcp-<system>-<suffix> with the system of this server and a suffix other than read, write and destructive (checked by the rule additional-group-valid), for example mcp-opensearch-ops for an ops-only tool. It can only narrow access (platform-call-additional-group); the risk-derived group is still needed. Part of definitionHash, so a change needs approval. Not allowed in an adapter manifest.

definitionHash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of kind, the members of definition, the entry fields and system, credential (CC-258). Receivers recompute it.

AdapterResourceTemplateEntry.description: Manifest entry of a resource template of an adapter (CC-258): variables carry maxLength and pattern instead of a type, no additionalGroup.

variables.description: One entry per variable of uriTemplate, in the order of first occurrence (rule uri-variables-bound).

definitionHash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of kind, the members of definition, the entry fields and system, credential (CC-258). Receivers recompute it.

McpPromptDefinition.description: MCP prompt definition as returned by prompts/list (CC-258). Every member is part of definitionHash; the messages are a field of the entry and are hashed too.

PromptEntry.description: Manifest entry of a prompt (CC-258). The prompt is data of the manifest: the gateway builds the result of prompts/get from messages and never calls the server. The author wraps an argument in markers (<ticket_id>{{ticketId}}</ticket_id>); the gateway refuses argument values with <, >, { or } at every prompts/get, whatever the pattern says. messages is removed from prompts/list.

argumentRules.description: One rule per argument of definition.arguments, no more and no fewer (rule prompts-valid).

pattern.description: Anchored like a pattern in inputSchema (CC-078, CC-123). TAB, LF and CR are forbidden in values with a pattern (README, 'Text hygiene'), so arguments are one line.

type.description: Optional resource type: the value must match its idPattern as well. May be a valueOnly type.

messages.description: Messages of the result of prompts/get; {{argument}} places a value, only names of definition.arguments (rule prompt-placeholders-declared).

additionalGroup.description: Optional group (C9) that a user needs in addition to the group the risk derives: mcp-<system>-<suffix> with the system of this server and a suffix other than read, write and destructive (checked by the rule additional-group-valid), for example mcp-opensearch-ops for an ops-only tool. It can only narrow access (platform-call-additional-group); the risk-derived group is still needed. Part of definitionHash, so a change needs approval. Not allowed in an adapter manifest.

definitionHash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of kind, the members of definition, argumentRules, messages, additionalGroup when present, system and credential (CC-258).

allOf.description: At least one of the four lists is not empty (CC-258): a manifest without any primitive is refused.
